extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic geometry; readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea'
extracted.subtask_description: List of desired properties, definitions, and key theorems about cohomology (Hi) of quasicoherent sheaves on schemes, especially projective/quasicompact separated schemes, as presented in Vakil's text. Includes vanishing theorems, functoriality, base change, explicit calculations on P^n, and related consequences (Serre vanishing, coherence of pushforwards, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality of Hi
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Hi is a covariant functor from QCoh(X) to Mod_A (for X a separated and quasicompact A-scheme).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as property (i). It means maps of sheaves induce maps on cohomology; used throughout (e.g., covariance for long exact sequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of H0 with global sections
rubrics_metrics.description: H0(X, F) is identified with the global section functor Γ(X, F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (ii). Covariance for i=0 is the usual covariance of Γ; many consequences follow from recognizing H0 as Γ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence in cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: A short exact sequence 0 → F → G → H → 0 of quasicoherent sheaves yields a long exact sequence ... → H^i(X,F) → H^i(X,G) → H^i(X,H) → H^{i+1}(X,F) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (iii). Connecting homomorphisms must be defined; exercises show how to construct them via Čech cohomology and check naturality/compatibility with localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality in the space (pullback/pushforward maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a morphism π: X → Y (quasicompact, separated), and F on X, there is a natural morphism Hi(Y, π_*F) → Hi(X, F) extending Γ; equivalently Hi is contravariant in the space via pullback adjunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (iv). This natural map is part of the Leray spectral sequence story; Exercises 18.2.E and 18.2.F ask to describe these maps explicitly using affine covers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine pushforward isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is affine (quasicompact, separated), then the natural map Hi(Y, π_*F) → Hi(X, F) is an isomorphism for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (v). Used to reduce cohomology calculations along affine morphisms and to translate problems on closed/projective embeddings to projective space computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine-cover cohomology vanishing
rubrics_metrics.description: If X can be covered by n affine open sets, then H^i(X, F) = 0 for all i ≥ n (in particular, on affine schemes H^i = 0 for i > 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (vi). This is the Čech-vanishing result proven by showing higher Čech cohomology vanishes for affine covers (Theorem 18.2.4). It implies Γ is exact on affines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dimensional cohomology vanishing (topological bound)
rubrics_metrics.description: If dim X = n then H^i(X, F) = 0 for all i > n for any quasicoherent sheaf F (proved for projective/quasiprojective k-schemes and more generally via derived functors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as part of (vi) and Theorem 18.2.6; note proof uses covering by n+1 affines or derived-functor arguments for broad generality. See 18.2.7 for wider generalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior under direct sums and filtered colimits
rubrics_metrics.description: Hi commutes with direct sums and, more generally, with filtered colimits: Hi(X, lim_Fj) = lim_Hi(X, Fj).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (vii). Exercise 18.2.G indicates this can be proved directly; in module categories filtered colimits are exact which is the key input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology of O(m) on P^n (explicit ranks/vanishing/duality)
rubrics_metrics.description: For projective space P^n_A and the line bundles O(m): H^0(P^n_A,O(m)) is a free A-module of rank (n+m choose m) for m ≥ 0; H^n(P^n_A,O(m)) is free of rank (−m−1 choose −n−m−1) for m ≤ −n−1; and H^i(P^n_A,O(m)) = 0 otherwise. There is a natural Serre duality pairing and the alternating sum (−1)^i dim H^i(P^n,O(m)) is a polynomial in m (first example of a Hilbert polynomial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property (viii) / Theorem 18.1.3. The text lists many consequences: finite generation, Kodaira-type vanishing for top cohomology when m > −n−1, appearance of dualizing sheaf for m = −n−1 (over a field), and Hilbert polynomial behaviour. Exercises 18.3.B–C show the Čech computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation/coherence of cohomology on projective schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian and F is a coherent sheaf on a projective A-scheme X, then Hi(X, F) is a coherent (finitely generated) A-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 18.1.4(i). Proof reduces to P^n_A and uses the long exact sequence together with the O(m) calculations; important for finiteness results like Corollary 18.1.5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre vanishing
rubrics_metrics.description: For F coherent on a projective A-scheme (A Noetherian) there exists N >> 0 such that for all m ≥ N, Hi(X, F(m)) = 0 for all i > 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 18.1.4(ii). The proof uses surjections from sums of O(m) and the vanishing results for O(m). A stronger version appears later (Theorem 18.8.G).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforwards of coherent sheaves by projective morphisms are coherent
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is projective and X, Y are locally Noetherian, then π_* of a coherent sheaf on X is coherent on Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given as 18.1.A (Crucial Exercise) with pointers to Grothendieck's Coherence Theorems 18.8.1 and 18.9.1 for generalizations. Used to deduce facts like finiteness of π_*OX and characterizations of finite morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective + finite fibers (quasi-finite) implies finite
rubrics_metrics.description: If π: X → Y is projective with Y Noetherian, then π is finite if and only if it is projective and has finite fibers (equivalently projective and quasi-finite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 18.1.8. Proof uses local affine neighborhoods and choosing hypersurfaces to reduce to the projective+affine case together with earlier corollaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomological criterion for affineness (Serre)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is quasicompact and quasiseparated and Hi(X, F) = 0 for all i > 0 and all quasicoherent F (or only H1 of every quasicoherent ideal sheaf vanishes), then X is affine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 18.1.1. This is the converse to affine-cover vanishing when n = 1; Vakil states he will not prove it here but references GW, Thm.12.35.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence of Čech cohomology from cover
rubrics_metrics.description: For a quasicompact separated scheme X, the cohomology Hi_U(X,F) computed from a finite affine cover U is independent of the chosen cover; hence define Hi(X,F) unambiguously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem/Definition 18.2.2. Proof reduces comparing covers differing by one open and uses vanishing of higher Čech cohomology on affines (Theorem 18.2.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher Čech cohomology vanishes on affines
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is an affine A-scheme and U is an affine cover, then Hi_U(X, F) = 0 for i > 0 and any quasicoherent F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 18.2.4. The proof uses localization to distinguished opens and a partition-of-unity-style argument (or spectral-sequence shortening). This is the technical heart allowing many reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base change for cohomology under field extension
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is a quasicompact separated k-scheme and K/k is a field extension, then Hi(X,F) ⊗_k K ≅ Hi(X ×_k Spec K, F ⊗_k K) for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 18.2.H. Useful for reducing statements over arbitrary fields to algebraically closed fields; the exercise also hints at more general flat-base-change statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base-point-freeness stable under field extension
rubrics_metrics.description: An invertible sheaf L on a k-scheme X is base-point-free iff its pullback to X ×_k Spec K is base-point-free for any field extension K/k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 18.2.I. Follows from base-change property for H0 (i=0) and the behavior of sections under tensoring with K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Künneth formula for cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are quasicompact separated k-schemes and F, G quasicoherent on X and Y, then H^m(X×Y, F ⊠ G) ≅ ⊕_{p+q=m} H^p(X,F) ⊗_k H^q(Y,G).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated in 18.2.8. Proof sketch: take affine covers of X and Y, form Čech complexes, and identify the total complex with the tensor product of complexes; use Eilenberg–Zilber-type result on homology of tensor products.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cup product existence
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a cup product in Čech cohomology with a simple construction (references given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned in 18.2.9; Vakil refers to Liu Ex.2.17 for an elegant description. No detailed construction given here, but the presence of cup product is an expected multiplicative structure on cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semicontinuity of fiber dimension for projective morphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For a projective morphism π: X → Y with Y locally Noetherian, the set { q ∈ Y : dim π^{-1}(q) > k } is Zariski-closed; fiber dimension is upper-semicontinuous on the target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 18.1.B. The proof uses the trick from Theorem 18.1.8 of choosing hypersurfaces to control images and supports geometric intuition about how fiber dimension 'jumps' on closed subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of finite flat morphism (rank of pushforward)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite flat morphism π: C → C' of irreducible curves, the degree of π is the rank of the locally free sheaf π_* O_C; equivalently degree of rational map equals rank of π_* O_C when curves are integral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 17.4.6 and Exercise 17.4.C. Remarks connect algebraic degree to analytic degree for complex curves (counting preimages with multiplicity), and exercises (17.4.D–F) examine fiber multiplicities, relation to valuations, and zeros/poles counts via degree of associated morphism to P^1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiber multiplicity accounting for degree
rubrics_metrics.description: For finite morphisms of curves, the number of points in the fiber counted with appropriate multiplicity (including contributions from nonreducedness and field extensions) equals the rank/degree d of π_* O_C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 17.4.5, Exercise 17.4.D, and discussion in 17.4.9 illustrate three behaviors in fibers: distinct rational points, nonreduced points (multiplicity), and field-extension-induced multiplicity; all contribute to the constant total d across fibers.
